investigation.method: manual review of the live website

headline: Milnrow Village Practice looks like a My Surgery Website build with PATCHS as a clearly signposted digital route, but only for non-urgent and routine requests. The appointments page also says all appointments will be by phone first, which makes the overall access model more phone-led than the GTD PATCHS sites.

live_stack.label: Public website stack
evidence: The footer says Built by My Surgery Website.
The site structure and widgets match the My Surgery Website pattern.

live_stack.label: Current online request platform for routine access
evidence: The homepage and online-services page link to https://patchs.ai/practice/milnrowvillagepractice.
The link is explicitly labelled PATCHS (online access) - NON URGENT/ROUTINE REQUESTS.

live_stack.label: Prescription-side legacy platform
evidence: The prescriptions page says repeat prescriptions can be ordered using the GP online system: EMIS Access.

current_routes.label: PATCHS direct route
notes: The website presents PATCHS as the route for non-urgent and routine requests, not obviously for every request type.

current_routes.label: Appointments workflow
notes: The appointments page says all appointments will be by phone first.
It also says patients can state a preference for phone, face-to-face, video call, text or email.

current_routes.label: Prescriptions
notes: The prescriptions page says repeat prescriptions can be ordered using the NHS App, EMIS Access or a paper slip.
It says repeat prescription requests are no longer accepted by telephone unless the patient is housebound, and then only after 14:00.
The page says to allow 48 working hours.

complaints_and_feedback.headline: The site has a feedback page, but it does not present a strong complaints route.

items.label: Feedback and complaints page
notes: The page is live, but the visible content leans heavily toward Friends and Family feedback, reviews and GP Patient Survey material.
A clear complaints process was not obvious during this pass.

items.label: Guessed NHS-style complaints path
notes: That common NHS-style complaints URL returns 404 here.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: PATCHS appears limited-scope
notes: PATCHS is clearly signposted, but only as the route for non-urgent and routine requests, so it does not look like the whole front door.

probably_true: Milnrow uses PATCHS for at least some digital access, but not as an all-purpose front door.
The public appointments model is notably more phone-led than the GTD sites reviewed so far.
needs_follow_up: How Milnrow handles urgent online demand, since PATCHS is labelled only for non-urgent and routine requests.
Whether there is a fuller complaints route that is simply not surfaced cleanly on the public site.
